lines.trans: Goodbye!

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian word for both casual 'yes / yeah' and 'oh! / ah!' upon noticing something.

examples.trans: Oh, the door opened! Thank you.
Yes, eight rooms and eight keys.

meanings.note: The color blue.

examples.trans: The blue suitcase is in the luggage closet.
I have two blue teacups.

meanings.note: Before an indefinite noun أول means 'first' (أول يوم 'first day'); after a definite noun الأول / الأولى agrees in gender (الصفحة الأولى 'the first page'). Also used adverbially ('first').

examples.trans: Welcome on your first day of work!
Read the first page calmly.

meanings.note: Name of the month of May in the Levantine calendar.

examples.trans: My birthday is in May.
In May the weather gets nice in Amman.

meanings.note: Core Jordanian everyday verb for 'to come' (إجا / بيجي).

examples.trans: You came ten minutes early.
I will come on Friday at noon.

meanings.note: Everyday conditional word 'if' for real possibilities.

examples.text: رني الجرس إذا احتجتي أي شي.
examples.trans: Ring the bell if you need anything.

examples.text: إذا فتحنا الساحة الصبح، الجيران بيفرحوا.
examples.trans: If we open the courtyard in the morning, the neighbours will be delighted.

meanings.note: Said on its own, اتفقنا ('we agreed') is the everyday way to close a deal: 'deal!'.

examples.text: اتفقنا، بنلتقي الساعة تسعة عند الباب.
examples.trans: Agreed, we meet at nine at the door.

examples.text: اتفقت مع سلمى على كيكة الجمعة.
examples.trans: I agreed with Salma about the Friday cake.

meanings.note: The holy day in Islam and the weekend in Jordan.

examples.trans: The family gathers every Friday at noon.
On Friday the street is quiet.

meanings.note: Signature Levantine word for 'want / need', inflected with pronoun suffixes: بدي (I want), بدك (you want), بده (he/it wants), بدها (she/it wants), بدنا (we want), بدكم (you pl. want), بدهم (they want).

examples.trans: I want to read the booking ledger.
Jam bread needs unsalted butter.

meanings.note: Extremely common Jordanian word meaning both 'only / just' (بس نص كاسة 'just half a glass') and 'but' between clauses.

examples.text: بدي أقرأ الدفتر، بس مش ملاقي نظارتي!
examples.trans: I want to read the ledger, only I cannot find my glasses!
Just half a glass, please.

meanings.note: Singular form for any type of card (ID, credit, ticket, etc.).

examples.trans: There is a paper tag on the suitcase.
I wrote my name on the card.

meanings.note: The musical instrument.

examples.trans: The sound of the piano is warm and calm.
I learned piano when I was young.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: بيوت.

examples.trans: The old house has a lovely courtyard.
The neighbourhood houses are built of stone.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: تانية, plural: تانيين).

examples.trans: Room four is on the second floor.
There is a second sheet behind the letter.

meanings.note: The number 9.

examples.trans: The quietness in the courtyard is nine out of ten!
She came back in just nine minutes!

meanings.note: The number 30.

examples.trans: They have given us thirty days in the letter.
The bill is thirty-eight dinars.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بجيب, بيجيب).

examples.text: رح أجيب شراشف نظيفة من الخزانة.
examples.trans: I will bring clean sheets from the closet.

examples.text: أي علبة زبدة جبتي يا نور؟
examples.trans: Which tub of butter did you bring, Nour?

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: جيران.

examples.trans: All the neighbours on the street are kind.
Good morning, dear neighbour.

meanings.note: Active participle of إجا ('to come'): means 'on the way / arriving' (جايين 'they are coming') and after a time noun 'next' (الأسبوع الجاي 'next week').

examples.trans: The guests are coming down the stairs now.
We will see you next week!

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بجمع, بيجمع).

examples.trans: Today our courtyard brings a family together!
We gathered the chairs under the tree.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb for 'to speak, talk, tell' (بحكي / حكى).

examples.trans: Salma chats with all the neighbours.
Tell me everything I need to know.

meanings.note: One of the most frequently used adjectives in Jordanian Arabic to mean beautiful, sweet, nice, or good.

examples.trans: The strawberry jam is sweet and tasty.
The sweater looks lovely and warm.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: خبازين.

examples.trans: The baker opens the oven at five in the morning.
The bakers' market is near the overpass.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: خطط.

examples.trans: What is your plan for tomorrow morning?
That is an excellent, practical plan.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بخبز, بيخبز).

examples.text: اخبزي قطع زوايا كتير يا سلمى!
examples.trans: Bake plenty of corner pieces, Salma!

examples.text: قديش بيقدر فرنك يخبز كل صبح؟
examples.trans: How much can your oven bake every morning?

meanings.note: Future tense marker in Jordanian and Levantine Arabic, equivalent to 'sa-' in MSA.

examples.text: ضيفة غرفة أربعة رح تقعد كل الأسبوع.
examples.trans: Room four's guest will stay all week.

examples.text: تاني يوم ما رح يكون ممل!
examples.trans: The second day is not going to be boring!

meanings.note: Refers to a corner of a room or street, or a geometric angle.

examples.trans: The corner shop opens early.
I love the corner pieces of lemon cake.

meanings.note: Everyday word for an hour of time, a wristwatch, or a wall clock.

examples.trans: What time is it right now, please?
We arrived an hour ago on the dot.

meanings.note: From سكت, to fall silent: a person who says nothing, or a thing that makes no sound.

examples.trans: Why are you so quiet today? Is something wrong?
The phone has been silent since the morning.

meanings.note: The number 6.

examples.trans: Room six is on the second floor.
I have six lemons in the basket.

meanings.note: Core word in مع السلامة! ('goodbye!', literally 'with safety') and الحمد لله عالسلامة ('glad you arrived safely').

examples.trans: Goodbye, see you tomorrow!
Thank goodness for your safe arrival.

meanings.note: Everyday word for a year.

examples.trans: The building is eighty years old.
I have not seen him for three years.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: شوارع.

examples.trans: Our guesthouse is on a quiet street in central Amman.
There are old stone streets in the quarter.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb for 'to see, look, check' (بشوف / شاف).

examples.trans: Look inside the suitcase, Nour!
I will see you tomorrow at breakfast.

meanings.note: A staple beverage in Jordanian culture, typically served with mint or sage.

examples.trans: Please have a glass of hot mint tea.
There is black tea and coffee at breakfast.

meanings.note: Singulative شجرة ('a tree', feminine), collective شجر ('trees').

examples.trans: We placed the table under the old tree.
We hear the rustle of tree leaves in the courtyard.

meanings.note: Everyday word for a month.

examples.trans: That was the best sleep in a month!
The contract renews at the start of next month.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian interrogative pronoun for 'what'.

examples.trans: What is that sound?
What is written on the sheet, Rami?

meanings.note: Levantine word for slatted window shutters, used as a collective: الشيش مسكر 'the shutters are closed'.

examples.trans: Close the shutters, the sun is strong.
Green shutters suit the house.

meanings.note: Transitive, with a doubled h (sahha): you wake someone else. Compare صحي, to wake up yourself.

examples.trans: Wake me up at six, please.
The bell woke all the guests.

meanings.note: Any picture or photograph; صورة أبيض وأسود is a black-and-white photo.

examples.trans: I took a nice photo of you in the courtyard.
I have old photos of my grandmother.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: طوابق.

examples.trans: Your room is on the second floor on the right.
The building has three storeys.

meanings.note: To paint a wall, door or shutter with a brush; the paint itself is دهان.

examples.trans: We painted the door blue last year.
We want to paint the children's room yellow.

meanings.note: The standalone number ten.

examples.trans: You arrived ten minutes early.
Breakfast is from seven-thirty to ten.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بعزف, بيعزف).

examples.trans: I am still waiting for you to play the scale!

examples.text: الكبير كان يعزف بيانو كل جمعة.
examples.trans: The older boy used to play piano every Friday.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian word for a room in a house or building.

examples.trans: We have eight comfortable rooms at the guesthouse.
Room four is ready and clean.

meanings.note: Wash dishes, clothes, windows or your hands.

examples.trans: I washed the cups and put them on the shelf.
Wash your hands before eating.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بفتح, بيفتح).

examples.trans: The corner shop opens at seven.
Oh, the door finally opened!

meanings.note: Mostly heard in من فضلك / من فضلكم, 'please', literally 'from your kindness'.

examples.trans: Excuse me, where is the station?
A glass of water, please.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بقول, بيقول).

examples.trans: What does clause fourteen say?
He said thank you and hung up!

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: قديمة, plural: قدام).

examples.trans: The courtyard has an old jasmine tree.
The old hardware shop is past the bridge.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بقرأ, بيقرأ).

examples.trans: I want to read the booking ledger.
Did you read the second page clipped underneath?

meanings.note: Refers to the material glass, a pane of glass, or sometimes a glass bottle.

examples.trans: Look at the courtyard through the window glass.
We wiped the glass this morning until it shone.

meanings.note: Past tense of 'to be' for 3rd person masculine singular. Widely used as an auxiliary verb.

examples.trans: How was the bus ride?

examples.text: تاني يوم ما رح يكون ممل!
examples.trans: The second day will not be boring!

meanings.note: An everyday item of furniture for sitting.

examples.trans: We placed eight chairs around the tables.
I tightened the screw on the wooden chair.

meanings.note: A highly versatile quantifier used to mean 'all of', 'every', or 'the whole'.

examples.trans: Tell me everything I need to know.
Everyone is happy in the courtyard today.

meanings.note: Refers generally to cake as a type of food.

examples.trans: I made chocolate cake for the kids.
Would you like a piece of cake with your tea?

meanings.note: Used to mark the limit of a time period, distance, or extent in colloquial Jordanian.

examples.trans: We waited until you called us.
I stayed up until midnight.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: لحظات.

examples.trans: Wait a moment, let me read the line.
We waited a moment by the gate.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: ليمون.

examples.trans: The warm lemon cake is ready.
I squeezed half a lemon into the soup.

meanings.note: Used mostly as a negative particle for verbs ('didn't') or as a relative pronoun/conjunction ('what' or 'that which').

examples.trans: Paper does not lose room names.
Have tea before you head out.

meanings.note: Polite everyday Jordanian address for an adult woman or female guest.

examples.trans: Good morning, madam, please come in!
The room is booked under Madam Suad.

meanings.note: Everyday preposition 'with'; takes pronoun suffixes to express 'have on one's person' (معي 'I have with me', معك حق 'you are right').

examples.trans: You are right, Nour!
Goodbye! (lit. go with safety)

meanings.note: In Jordanian speech, يا معلم is an affectionate, respectful way to address a boss or skilled craftsperson.

examples.trans: You are all generosity, boss!
She was a very gifted piano teacher.

meanings.note: Means both a door key and a mechanic's spanner/wrench (مفتاح حديد iron wrench).

examples.trans: Here is the key to room four.
We have eight brass keys on the board.

meanings.note: Often used as a noun meaning 'letter' (mail) or 'destiny' in traditional contexts.

examples.trans: What is written in the letter, Nour?
Our two names are still written in pencil.

meanings.note: One of the most basic Arabic prepositions indicating origin.

examples.trans: I am Salma from the kitchen.
Breakfast is from seven-thirty to ten.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: ناس.

examples.trans: You are kind, generous people.
Morning coffee brings people together in the courtyard.

meanings.note: Extremely common word used in time (e.g., 3 and a half) and measurements.

examples.trans: Breakfast starts at seven thirty.

examples.text: بس نص كاسة عصير لو سمحت.
examples.trans: Just half a glass of juice, please.

meanings.note: Standard adverb for physical location.

examples.trans: Here we use this big ledger.
Stay right here a minute.

meanings.note: Very common spatial preposition in Jordanian Arabic.

examples.trans: Look in the mirror behind the desk.
The hardware shop is past the bridge.

meanings.note: Vocative particle used when addressing someone directly.

examples.trans: Good morning, Tariq!
Oh, how lovely the sun is after the rain!

meanings.note: Very common interjection used to urge action or to say goodbye ('yalla bye').

examples.trans: Come on, let us bring the bag down into the light!
Let us go check out the room right now!

meanings.note: Standard noun for day, often used in expressions like 'el-yom' (today).

examples.trans: Today the weather is sunny and warm in Amman.
Have a happy, successful day!
